name: the Stone Age
summary: Wild woodland, muddy tracks and hide shelters gather around the Chief's communal bonfire.

rules.roads: Use an uneven, trampled mud track running along x, 8 m wide within |z| <= 4. Street dressing: 14 parts, all below 1.2 m, comprising shallow wheel-free drag grooves, footprints, puddles, embedded stones and broken twigs. Concentrate solid clutter near the margins and keep the middle unobstructed. No paving, straight drainage channels or engineered road edges.
rules.walkingEdge: The strips at |z| 4–6 are irregular earth, moss and flattened vegetation, not pavements. Walking simply spills onto this ground. Trees, arrival markers and corner lights can occupy z 5 without implying a constructed sidewalk.
rules.lotMarkers: Free lot: 10 parts on an unclaimed 16 m parcel, with the marker near x 4.5, z 4.5. Two crooked sticks support a large empty twig loop thickened with mud and pale ochre; its visibly vacant centre is the wordless available symbol used throughout the ages. Add a few stones and tufts, never a sign board. Community lot: 14 parts, with four corner stones and a front forked-stick marker bearing four small clay impressions around one shared centre; this means collective building rather than private availability. Keep the project area empty.
rules.boundaries: Claimed lot: 24 parts including its owner marker. Use irregular low stakes, loose branches, hide ties and occasional boulders along z -6 and x -6, approximately 0.6–0.9 m high and always below 1.2 m. Keep the +z frontage open with a clear entrance gap. This is an occupied camp enclosure, not a picket fence.
rules.ownerMarker: At the front corner, lash a mud-daubed bark patch to a crooked post. An owner-colour tie in #d9534f and a filled clan emblem distinguish it from the empty free-lot loop. Show the exact player name as a restrained gameplay label anchored to the patch; do not invent alphabetic Stone Age signage.
rules.lighting: Street light: 8 parts at x 0, z 5, comprising an uneven stake, fork, hide bindings, a resinous bark bundle and chunky flame shapes. Flame and ember parts use glow=true; wood and bindings do not. These are hand-tended gathering-point torches, not a regular municipal lighting installation.
rules.centrepiece: Square centrepiece: 34 parts within a roughly 4.5 m diameter. Build a communal bonfire from irregular standing and fallen logs, a broken ring of stones, chunky flame wedges and three short log seats. Only flame and ember parts use glow=true. Keep flames broad and low enough that people behind remain visible; no fountain basin or hidden modern fountain silhouette.
rules.seating: Use 5 parts for a broad fallen log with a roughly flattened sitting face, two stone chocks and a split bark end. Seat height is about 0.45 m, with room for two. No legs cut to furniture precision, backrest slats or metal fittings.
rules.market: Use 20 parts within about 2.6 × 1.6 m: an irregular hide spread directly on the ground, stone corner weights, shallow woven baskets, berries, flint blanks, antler tools and wrapped bundles. The trader kneels beside the goods. No elevated sales counter, roof frame or coins.
rules.trees: Street pair: 24 parts total, at x -3 and x 3, z 5; use a leaning birch with a torn, sparse crown and a shorter crooked pine with one heavy side. They are surviving wild growth beside a track, not deliberately planted street trees. Wild group: 34 parts for a tall wind-bent pine, a broad uneven birch and a squat juniper bush. Vary trunk angles, branch lengths, crown heights and foliage masses; never use centred lollipop crowns. Countryside dressing: 14 low, scattered parts made from grass tussocks, loose flint, moss patches, two broken branches and shallow puddles; keep them sparse and mostly below 0.35 m.
rules.arrival: Use 58 parts including the vehicle and stop. At z 5 place a forked arrival stake with a knotted hide pennant and a flattened waiting patch, not a platform. At z 0, aligned along x, place a toy-compressed mammoth-drawn wooden sledge approximately 5 m long overall. Give the mammoth a shaggy stepped silhouette, unequal tusks and a hide harness; the sledge has runners, lashings and bundled passengers' goods, never wheels.
rules.crossing: Use 42 parts for stepping boulders and a fallen-log crossing within a 4 m-wide corridor running along z. Several broad fallen trunks bridge between natural rock supports, with flat stones filling walkable gaps; retain a continuous traversable route without modern decking or rails. Water runs along x and occupies |z| <= 7; the tile displays its central 12 m, while bank landings belong at z ±7 in the adjoining bank sections. Meet the banks about 1 m above water. Add reeds, exposed roots and uneven rocks, not masonry abutments.
rules.camp: Use 72 parts for two hide tents, a branch windbreak, a stone-ringed fire, flint and hide bundles, and a resting mammoth beside its sledge across the east river. Only fire and embers use glow=true. The separate caravan-leader figure uses 34 parts including the base body: a mammoth herder in a patchwork fur wrap, weathered hood and braided belt, carrying a hooked wooden staff. Pale exotic shell beads and a hide bundle with an unfamiliar clan emblem say the herder has travelled far.
rules.people: Use 44 parts total for two residents at x -0.6 and x 0.6, retaining the supplied blocky base bodies. One wears a sleeveless hide wrap, uneven fur boots and tied dark hair and carries a stone adze; the other wears a woven-grass cape over a hide skirt, loose hair and carries a gathering basket. Use convincing clothing construction rather than generic ragged caveman costumes.
rules.head: The Chief uses 38 parts including the base figure. Give them a broad layered hide mantle, an asymmetric antler-and-feather headdress, ochre face marks and an oversized bone-topped wooden staff. The large headdress and staff must identify the office at stream scale; no metal crown, throne-room robes or modern mayoral sash.

designDirection: Build bright, chunky low-poly toys for a roughly 40° overhead view, using irregular silhouettes rather than fine texture to express age. Preserve the 5×5 block plan, 16 m parcels, four community lots around the central square, and caravan camp beyond the river east of the ring road; transformations retain footprint and purpose. Translate every request through communal shelter, hand tools, gathered materials and fire, with mammoth transport as the setting's deliberate prehistoric fantasy. A skyscraper becomes stepped rock-and-log clan lodging, a car becomes a lashed hauling sledge, and a café becomes a hide shelter serving warm broth beside embers. Keep open entrances, readable owner accents and strong vacant-loop versus occupied-emblem silhouettes throughout.

name: the Bronze Age
summary: Sun-baked mudbrick, reed shade and bronze sun emblems surround the High Priest's communal well.

rules.roads: Use compacted ochre earth along x, 8 m wide within |z| <= 4, with pale dust on high spots and darker compressed cart routes. Street dressing: 16 parts below 1.2 m, including shallow wheel ruts, hoof impressions, flush stone patches, puddles and fragments of open terracotta runoff channels near the edges. Keep the central walking route clear. Do not turn the whole town into a paved classical city.
rules.walkingEdge: At |z| 4–6, provide flush, swept earth frontage with occasional reed mats and irregular doorstep stones. These are not continuous pavements, and there is no raised kerb. Trees and corner fixtures at z 5 stand in this shared frontage.
rules.lotMarkers: Free lot: 12 parts on the 16 m parcel, with a forked timber post near x 4.5, z 4.5 holding a large sun-dried clay ring painted pale ochre. The empty centre continues the wordless available symbol; add pottery fragments, dry grass and a small stone weight. Community lot: 16 parts, with four low mudbrick corner markers and a front clay medallion showing four impressed dots around a shared central bowl. Keep its interior clear for a public project.
rules.boundaries: Claimed lot: 28 parts including the name marker. Use a low mudbrick footing with short woven-reed or wattle panels along z -6 and x -6, 0.7–0.95 m high and never above 1.2 m. Leave the +z frontage open with a gap between two thicker gate posts. Use hand-formed, slightly irregular brick courses rather than modern garden walls.
rules.ownerMarker: Hang an incised clay name tablet from the front gate post with fibre cord. Paint a broad band on the post in owner colour #d9534f and use a filled household seal. Display the exact player name as a gameplay label anchored to the tablet, avoiding fake historical script or a modern printed board.
rules.lighting: Street light: 12 parts at x 0, z 5, with a short mudbrick pedestal, timber fork and large shallow ceramic oil bowl. Flame parts use glow=true; oil vessels and bronze trim remain unlit. These are attended civic or temple-corner lamps, not electric-looking lamps distributed at mechanical intervals.
rules.centrepiece: Use 38 parts for a communal well court about 4.5 m across. A low limestone wellhead, timber rope beam, wooden bucket, four pottery water jars and shallow stone collection basins form the gathering place. A modest hammered-bronze sun disc marks the High Priest's civic stewardship. No powered jet, Roman fountain sculpture or unnecessary glow.
rules.seating: Use 6 parts for a broad limestone sitting slab on two low rubble-and-mudbrick supports, with a thin reed sitting mat. The top is about 0.45 m high and accommodates two people. Keep it heavy, simple and slightly uneven.
rules.market: Use 28 parts within 2.6 × 1.6 m: four forked timber uprights, a sloping reed-mat roof, a mudbrick display ledge, woven grain baskets, pottery jars, linen bundles and a few bronze ingots. Goods are traded with weights or barter rather than modern tills and price labels.
rules.trees: Street pair: 26 parts total at x -3 and x 3, z 5, consisting of a watered fig with a broad crown leaning away from its trunk and a younger date palm with unequal fronds and an off-centre crown. Small earthen watering basins replace metal tree grilles. Wild group: 34 parts for a tall irregular tamarisk, a broad carob and a low thorn bush. Countryside dressing: 14 sparse parts of dry grass, barley stubble, smooth limestone, fallen reed stems and a few potsherds, mostly below 0.35 m. Maintain asymmetry even in tended planting.
rules.arrival: Use 58 parts for a chariot arrival place and its rig. At z 5, place a carved tether stone, a reed shade and a clay wheel emblem; there is no raised transit platform. A horse and light two-wheeled chariot wait at z 0, aligned along x and toy-compressed to about 5 m overall. Use a wooden body, leather lashings and bronze fittings, without saddles, stirrups or iron chassis.
rules.crossing: Use 54 parts for a 4 m-wide limestone crossing running along z, built from several short corbelled arches on squat stone piers rather than a Roman semicircular arch. The deck meets each bank about 1 m above water, with low stone edge blocks. Water flows along x across |z| <= 7; show the central 12 m in the river tile and place true bank landings at z ±7 in its continuations. Dress banks with reeds, mud steps, jars and mooring stones. Keep the span continuous and walkable.
rules.camp: Use 80 parts for two shallow-draft trading barges moored at the far bank, each with a reed awning, plus one shore-side reed shelter. Add amphora-like storage jars, grain sacks, folded textiles, a balance scale and a ceramic hearth; hearth flames use glow=true. The separate caravan leader uses 36 parts including the base figure: a river trader in a striped wool mantle, wrapped linen headcloth and leather sandals, carrying a small balance. A lapis-coloured bead collar and unfamiliar woven border identify distant trading connections.
rules.people: Use 46 parts total for two residents at x -0.6 and x 0.6, retaining the base bodies. One wears a linen wrap skirt, short wool shoulder cloth and tied hair and carries a pottery jar; the other wears a knee-length belted tunic, a sun headcloth and sandals and carries a bronze-bladed hoe. Clothing is layered, dyed sparingly and clearly constructed from woven cloth.
rules.head: The High Priest uses 40 parts including the base figure. Use a long cream linen robe, an ochre-and-turquoise woven mantle, a wrapped ceremonial headdress and a large hammered-bronze sun disc on the chest. A tall wooden staff capped with a second simple sun emblem makes the office readable from above. Avoid medieval crowns, mitres and unrelated monumental-civilisation costume mixtures.

designDirection: Use a coherent late-Bronze eastern Mediterranean river-town vocabulary: bright sun-baked masses, reed shade, woven cloth and small bronze accents, all rendered as chunky toys for the 40° overhead camera. Preserve the 5×5 block plan, 16 m parcels, four central community lots and camp beyond the east river, with every transformed asset retaining its footprint and role. Replace prehistoric improvisation with measured craft and civic ritual, but do not jump ahead to a classical stone city. A skyscraper becomes a stepped mudbrick lodging-and-storehouse compound, a car becomes a light two-wheeled cart, and a café becomes a shaded barley-bread and broth court. Use broad clay silhouettes and occasional sun discs rather than coating every object in shiny metal.

name: the Middle Ages
summary: Cobblestone lanes, timber craft and heraldic cloth gather beneath the King's market cross.

rules.roads: Use irregular rounded cobblestones along x, 8 m wide within |z| <= 4, with muddy joints and worn cart routes. Street dressing: 20 low parts below 1.2 m, including shallow edge gutters, replacement stones, damp patches, wheel wear and a few low hitching stones. Keep the centre free of obstacles. The road is unmistakably cobbled, not flat modern paving or industrial rectangular setts.
rules.walkingEdge: At |z| 4–6, cobbles thin into irregular packed-earth frontage and isolated threshold slabs. There is no continuous raised sidewalk and no kerb. A shallow open gutter can follow the road margin, but it must remain flush and walkable; fixtures at z 5 occupy the shared frontage.
rules.lotMarkers: Free lot: 12 parts on the 16 m parcel, with a pegged timber post and an uneven wooden board near x 4.5, z 4.5. Paint one large pale-ochre empty ring on the board so availability reads without words; add grass, a small stone and a discarded wood offcut. Community lot: 16 parts, with four low fieldstone corner markers and a front timber tablet bearing four painted dots around a shared central rosette. No private heraldic shield on the community marker.
rules.boundaries: Claimed lot: 30 parts including the owner marker. Use low wattle panels between oak posts, with occasional rough-stone footings along z -6 and x -6. Keep everything 0.7–1.0 m high and below 1.2 m. Leave the +z frontage open with a clear entrance gap and a short gate post, not a continuous front wall.
rules.ownerMarker: Hang a small wooden shield from the front post, with a broad owner-colour field in #d9534f and a simple filled household emblem. Put the exact owner name on a pale painted strip across the shield in broad hand-painted lettering. The shield must remain subordinate to the building, not become a giant advertising sign.
rules.lighting: Street light: 14 parts at x 0, z 5. A stout oak post and short iron bracket carry a sheltered oil lantern with horn panels and a pitched cap. Only its flame uses glow=true; horn panels can be translucent but are not independent emitters. Use sparse watched lamps at important corners rather than Victorian rows of elaborate lamp standards.
rules.centrepiece: Use 44 parts for a market cross approximately 4.5 m across at its stepped base. Build broad worn stone steps, a short octagonal shaft and a simple cross finial, with small baskets and a public-notice tablet tucked against the base. Keep the whole monument about 2.5 m high so it remains readable without hiding the square. It is the market's meeting landmark, not a modern fountain or a monumental church spire.
rules.seating: Use 8 parts for a thick oak plank bench on two trestles, with visible wooden pegs and one slightly uneven brace. Seat height is about 0.45 m and width suits two people. Keep it backless and sturdy, without cast-iron park-bench ends.
rules.market: Use 30 parts within 2.6 × 1.6 m: a pegged timber counter, two tall uprights, a madder-red and cream striped cloth awning, bread rounds, cheeses, apples, wool rolls and woven baskets. Stripes are broad enough to read on stream. No tomatoes, potatoes, coffee machines or printed packaging.
rules.trees: Street pair: 28 parts total at x -3 and x 3, z 5; use an old pollarded lime with uneven regrowth and a smaller pear tree leaning toward the road. Neither has a centred ball crown or matching height. Wild group: 36 parts for a tall crooked oak, a broad hawthorn and a low holly or young hazel. Countryside dressing: 14 sparse low parts of nettle clumps, meadow flowers, mossy stones, split deadwood and shallow puddles, mostly below 0.35 m.
rules.arrival: Use 62 parts for a horse-cart arrival point. A timber hitching rail and hanging wheel emblem stand at z 5 on worn earth, without a platform or bus shelter. At z 0, aligned along x, place a horse and wooden passenger cart approximately 5 m long overall, with iron-rimmed wheels, a curved cloth cover and bundled luggage. Keep the horse and harness chunky, with no modern vehicle chassis hidden underneath.
rules.crossing: Use 64 parts for a timber drawbridge carried by squat stone piers, with a fixed approach at each end and a short central lifting section shown lowered. The crossing runs along z, is about 4 m wide and meets the banks roughly 1 m above water; low timber rails preserve visibility. Water flows along x across |z| <= 7, with only its central 12 m shown in the river tile and landings at z ±7 in bank continuations. Add a compact lifting frame, chains, reeds, river rocks and stone pier noses. No enormous gatehouse blocking the town.
rules.camp: Use 86 parts for a travelling court across the river: two heraldic cloth pavilions and one supply awning, a packhorse, a small baggage wagon, chests and a communal brazier. Include simple knight and minstrel camp cameos, with shield and lute silhouettes; brazier coals use glow=true. The separate caravan leader uses 38 parts including the base figure: a jester in two-colour motley, a three-point cloth cap with small bells and curled soft shoes, carrying a carved fool's baton. An unfamiliar court badge and travel patches make the jester visibly foreign to the town.
rules.people: Use 48 parts total for two residents at x -0.6 and x 0.6, retaining the base bodies. One wears a belted wool tunic, hose, a hood pushed back and leather shoes and carries a carpenter's mallet; the other wears a long wool dress, linen coif and work apron and carries a round loaf. Use varied hair and silhouettes, not two recoloured copies.
rules.head: The King uses 44 parts including the base figure. Give them a broad gold crown, a deep blue tunic, a red cloak with a simplified pale fur edge, a large clasp and a short ceremonial sceptre. The crown and cape establish rank instantly. Keep the body blocky and friendly, avoiding realistic armour detail or a silhouette indistinguishable from the caravan's knight.

designDirection: Use a coherent late-medieval river market town, with chunky oak frames, pale stone, slate or clay roofs and bold cloth accents, readable from the bright 40° overhead view. Preserve the 5×5 plan, 16 m lots, four central community parcels and camp across the east river, retaining every asset's footprint and purpose through transformation. Let guild craft, household heraldry and shared market life replace Bronze Age sun ritual without introducing industrial civic furniture. A skyscraper becomes a stepped timber-and-stone lodging tower, a car becomes a covered horse wagon, and a café becomes a bread-and-ale cookshop with an open serving hatch. Keep streets genuinely cobbled and shared by feet and carts, with irregular frontage rather than an anachronistic pavement network.

name: the Industrial Age
summary: Brick, iron, gaslight and steam make a proud civic town under the Alderman's chain of office.

rules.roads: Use dark rectangular granite setts along x, 8 m wide within |z| <= 4. Street dressing: 24 parts below 1.2 m, including flush drain grates, wheel-polished strips, damp patches, sandstone kerb sections and a few short iron bollards at the margins. Where tram track is needed, embed two grooved rails flush with the surface along x. Keep the middle traversable and omit painted traffic lanes.
rules.walkingEdge: Continuous flagstone pavements occupy |z| 4–6, raised about 0.12 m above the setts, with clearly cut kerbs and narrow road-side gutters. This is the first age with a deliberate municipal sidewalk system. Fixtures at z 5 stand on slabs; keep a usable route past them.
rules.lotMarkers: Free lot: 14 parts on a 16 m parcel, with a bolted iron post near x 4.5, z 4.5 supporting a cream enamel plate bearing a large ochre empty ring. The vacant centre, not text, signals availability; add brick fragments, ballast and sparse weeds. Community lot: 18 parts, with four low brick corner plinths and a front cast-iron public-works medallion showing four nodes around a central civic disc. Keep construction ground open.
rules.boundaries: Claimed lot: 34 parts including the owner marker. Use a low red-brick footing and simple cast-iron rail panels along z -6 and x -6, with total height around 0.9 m and always below 1.2 m. Leave the +z frontage open with a gap between short gate posts. Avoid dense spear forests and full-height factory fencing.
rules.ownerMarker: Mount a small enamel nameplate with a brass border on the front gate post. The post cap or broad enamel strip uses #d9534f, and the exact player name is set in clear, period-compatible painted lettering. Exposed bolts and a filled oval household emblem distinguish ownership from the free-lot ring.
rules.lighting: Street light: 16 parts at x 0, z 5, comprising a fluted cast-iron post, simple square lantern cage, glass panels and gas burner. Only the compact gas flame or mantle uses glow=true. Keep the silhouette upright and civic, with restrained ornament rather than miniature lacework.
rules.centrepiece: Use 52 parts for a cast-iron fountain on a stone plinth about 4.5 m across. A broad lower basin, short fluted column, shallow upper bowl and four modest spouts establish municipal pride. Use dark painted iron, brass fittings and visible blue water; water is not emissive. Keep the fountain around 2.4 m high and avoid decorative gears that serve no purpose.
rules.seating: Use 14 parts for a two-person bench with simplified cast-iron end frames and warm timber seat and back slats. Seat height is approximately 0.45 m. Broad curves and a few bolts are enough; do not model fine filigree.
rules.market: Use 34 parts within about 2.6 × 1.6 m: a timber barrow with two large iron-rimmed wheels, a folding canvas cover, an iron handle and a display of bread, tins, bundled newspapers and paper-wrapped goods. It is a movable street trader's barrow, not a medieval fixed striped stall or a plastic kiosk.
rules.trees: Street pair: 30 parts total at x -3 and x 3, z 5, with a slightly leaning young plane tree and a shorter elm with an uneven spreading crown. Give them low iron root guards and small pavement openings, not identical topiary. Wild group: 36 parts for a tall ash, a broad mature elm and a scrubby young birch. Countryside dressing: 16 low sparse parts of coarse grass, wildflowers, gravel, a few cinders and isolated sleeper offcuts near railway influence; keep most countryside healthy and readable rather than buried in soot.
rules.arrival: Use 68 parts for a short steam tram and its stop. At z 5 place an iron stop pole with an enamel tram-wheel emblem, a simple timetable case and a narrow canopy. At z 0, aligned along x, place a toy-compressed 5 m steam tram with a short boiler compartment, chimney, large exposed wheels and a timber passenger cabin. Rails are flush with the road. A tiny steam puff may suggest motion, but no opaque smoke plume may hide the town.
rules.crossing: Use 68 parts for a riveted iron viaduct crossing along z, about 4 m wide, with shallow lattice girders, stone piers and a timber carriage deck. The deck meets banks about 1 m above water, and side rails remain low and open. Water runs along x across |z| <= 7; show the central 12 m in the river tile and continue to real bank landings at z ±7. Add stone pier noses, gravel, mooring rings and a few reeds. Use structural ironwork, not decorative steampunk machinery.
rules.camp: Use 88 parts for two luxurious railway carriages serving as shelters, a striped veranda awning, a compact locomotive or tender, luggage trunks, coal baskets and a gas-lit gathering table across the river. Put them on a short siding that visibly continues off the camp tile; the train must not sit inexplicably on grass. Lamp flames use glow=true. The separate railway-baron leader uses 40 parts including the base figure: a cream travel coat, waistcoat, bowler, leather gloves and a pocket-watch chain, carrying a rolled railway concession map. Foreign railway crests and trunk labels imply a distant network.
rules.people: Use 48 parts total for two residents at x -0.6 and x 0.6, retaining the base bodies. One wears a flat cap, rolled shirt sleeves, waistcoat and heavy boots and carries a small tool case; the other wears a long practical skirt, fitted jacket and pinned hair and carries a ledger. Distinguish working roles without making everyone a soot-covered factory worker.
rules.head: The Alderman uses 42 parts including the base figure. Give them a tall black top hat, dark frock coat, waistcoat, polished boots and an oversized brass civic chain with one broad medallion. Carry a rolled town charter. The top hat and chain are the dominant office symbols, clearly different from the railway baron's travel coat and bowler.

designDirection: Build a bright late-19th-century civic town with red brick, disciplined street edges, dark iron and warm brass, using chunky silhouettes suitable for the 40° overhead view. Preserve the 5×5 grid, 16 m parcels, four central community lots and camp beyond the east river, with upgrades keeping the same footprint and service. Industrialisation should appear as standardised fabrication, public infrastructure and steam transport rather than arbitrary gears attached to older objects. A skyscraper becomes a stepped brick-and-iron commercial building, a car becomes a glazed horse cab, and a café becomes a tiled tea room with an enamel sign and timber shopfront. Keep daylight generous, smoke minimal and ironwork broad enough to read without visual noise.

name: the Modern Age
summary: Asphalt, clear signage and leafy public space frame the Mayor's welcoming, everyday town.

rules.roads: Use smooth charcoal asphalt along x, 8 m wide within |z| <= 4. Street dressing: 26 low parts below 1.2 m, including flat white lane dashes, a short pedestrian crossing near a junction, flush drain grates, patched asphalt and simple margin bollards. Keep the central route free of raised obstructions; paint is surface-flat. Use crisp but sparse markings so the town remains readable.
rules.walkingEdge: Concrete slab pavements occupy |z| 4–6 with a consistent 0.12 m kerb, narrow gutters and lowered crossing points. Tree pits and fixtures sit at z 5 while leaving circulation around them. Use simple contemporary details, not Victorian railings or decorative cobbled frontage.
rules.lotMarkers: Free lot: 12 parts on a 16 m parcel, with a compact recycled panel on a square post near x 4.5, z 4.5. A large amber empty ring on a pale field provides the wordless available signal; optional small text must not carry the meaning. Add sparse grass and two gravel patches. Community lot: 16 parts, with four low corner blocks and a green municipal marker bearing four nodes around one shared centre, plus a simple building-hand pictogram. Keep the interior clear for collaborative construction.
rules.boundaries: Claimed lot: 28 parts including the owner marker. Use low horizontal timber slats between powder-coated metal posts along z -6 and x -6, around 0.85 m high and below 1.2 m. Leave the +z front open with a clear gate gap. Keep spacing open enough to see the build beyond.
rules.ownerMarker: Mount a clean, modest rectangular nameplate on the front post with an owner-colour strip in #d9534f and a filled circular household emblem. Print the exact player name in large, simple lettering. Avoid estate-agent branding, giant billboards or unnecessary illuminated screens.
rules.lighting: Street light: 12 parts at x 0, z 5. Use a slim powder-coated pole, short curved arm and flat LED head with a broad underside diffuser. Only the diffuser uses glow=true. The shape must read as contemporary street infrastructure rather than a gas lamp with a white bulb.
rules.centrepiece: Use 48 parts for a low circular civic fountain about 4.5 m across, with pale concrete coping, a shallow blue basin and three short water jets. Add a simple offset stone form rather than historic statuary. Recessed pool-light lenses use glow=true; water and jets do not. Keep the centre low, accessible and visibly distinct from the Industrial Age's tiered cast-iron fountain.
rules.seating: Use 12 parts for a two-person bench with broad timber slats, a simple aluminium frame and a shallow backrest. Seat height is about 0.45 m. Add one arm divider only if it does not reduce the clear two-person reading; avoid ornate iron ends.
rules.market: Use 32 parts within 2.6 × 1.6 m for a compact kiosk with a flat overhang, powder-coated panels, a glass display, a service hatch and visible fruit crates, pastries and refill bottles. Use clear blocks of colour and unbranded packaging. The stall is a little contemporary shop, not a medieval canopy with a cash register added.
rules.trees: Street pair: 30 parts total at x -3 and x 3, z 5; use a tall plane tree with a subtly bent trunk and a smaller maple with an uneven crown and one low branch. Place them in separate permeable tree pits, not matching circular planters. Wild group: 38 parts for a tall oak, a broad willow and a flowering shrub. Countryside dressing: 14 sparse low parts of meadow flowers, grass clumps, fallen twigs, rounded stones and occasional shallow rain puddles, mostly below 0.35 m. Municipal care never means identical trees.
rules.arrival: Use 64 parts for a bus stop and short city minibus. At z 5 place a narrow transparent shelter, small seat and pole with a large bus pictogram. At z 0, aligned along x, place a roughly 5 m minibus with a recognisable windscreen, side windows, rubber tyres and an opening-side door facing the stop. Keep the boarding route clear and do not let the shelter consume the full walking strip.
rules.crossing: Use 58 parts for a simple precast-concrete road bridge running along z, about 4 m wide, with shallow beams, modest concrete abutments and open metal rails. Its deck meets the banks about 1 m above water. Water runs along x across |z| <= 7; the river tile shows its central 12 m and the real bank landings continue to z ±7. Add natural reed pockets, stones and small rainwater outlets without litter or excessive civil-engineering clutter.
rules.camp: Use 82 parts for a tourist coach, two broad parasol shelters and one small check-in awning across the river. Include luggage, a cooler, folding tables, a route display and a portable gathering light whose diffuser uses glow=true. The separate tour-guide leader uses 36 parts including the base figure: a bright practical jacket, bucket hat, neck lanyard and walking shoes, carrying a folded map. A suitcase with distant destination stickers and a contrasting regional scarf communicate travel without stereotypes.
rules.people: Use 46 parts total for two residents at x -0.6 and x 0.6, retaining the base bodies. One wears a hoodie, cropped trousers, trainers and loose textured hair and carries a small potted plant; the other wears a work jacket, jeans, sturdy shoes and tied-back hair and carries a phone. Use distinct body-accessory silhouettes, everyday fabrics and no brand logos.
rules.head: The Mayor uses 38 parts including the base figure. Give them a smart contemporary suit, a broad civic sash, a simple town badge and distinctive neat hair. Carry oversized rounded ceremonial ribbon scissors beside a short ribbon loop. The sash and scissors establish the office; do not retain the Alderman's top hat or heavy brass chain.

designDirection: Make a friendly present-day small town from clear contemporary forms, healthy planting and restrained civic graphics, rendered as bright low-poly toys from the 40° overhead camera. Preserve the 5×5 block plan, 16 m parcels, four community project lots and camp across the river beyond the east ring road, with every upgrade retaining its footprint and purpose. Replace industrial ornament with accessible public space, mass-produced components and recognisable everyday services rather than simply painting old assets white. A skyscraper becomes a stepped steel-and-concrete tower, a car becomes a compact hatchback, and a café becomes a glass-fronted espresso bar with a small service terrace. Keep traffic markings flat, colour accents purposeful and signs readable by silhouette before text.

name: the Wasteland
summary: Rust, scrap and dust surround the Overseer's fire barrel as armoured convoys bring supplies.

rules.roads: Use surviving cracked asphalt buried under a thin, uneven film of dust, running along x, 8 m wide within |z| <= 4. Street dressing: 22 parts, all below 1.2 m, comprising broad flush repair plates, shallow sand drifts, a few subdued cracks, worn tyre tracks, clogged gutter mouths and broken kerb sections near the margins. Keep the middle continuously clear and traversable. Road paint has disappeared beneath wear and dust; no fresh lane markings, luminous seams or road-spanning barricades. Cracks and patches stay close to the road's base value rather than forming a busy black web.
rules.walkingEdge: The strips at |z| 4–6 are remnants of concrete pavements, repaired with scavenged slabs and compacted grit. Retain intermittent worn kerbs about 0.08 m high, with flush sand-filled transitions wherever slabs are missing. These are maintained survivor footpaths through inherited ruins, not pristine municipal sidewalks. Keep a continuous usable walking route past fixtures at z 5; no open pits, exposed reinforcing spikes or obstructive rubble heaps.
rules.lotMarkers: Free lot: 12 parts on an unclaimed 16 m parcel. Near x 4.5, z 4.5, mount a large empty scrap-steel hoop on a crooked timber post with a bolted metal brace; a broad faded-ochre band makes the vacant centre readable without words. Add a low concrete fragment, two dry tufts, a timber offcut and shallow dust patches, leaving the parcel usable. Community lot: 18 parts, comprising four low corner markers made from concrete chunks and short scrap stakes, a front marker assembled from a salvaged hatch panel, and sparse flat ground repairs. Paint four ochre nodes around one shared central disc on the panel, with a simple building-hand pictogram below. This denotes a collective project, not private availability; keep the interior empty.
rules.boundaries: Claimed lot: 32 parts including the owner marker. Alternate low corrugated-metal panels, scrap-timber rails, tyre sections and short sandbag footings along z -6 and x -6. Use deliberate repairs and broad material changes rather than random rubbish. Boundaries are about 0.7–0.95 m high and always below 1.2 m, with gaps that preserve views of the build. Keep the +z frontage open, with a clear entrance gap between two mismatched reinforced posts; no full perimeter fortress, razor wire or sharpened stakes.
rules.ownerMarker: Bolt a flattened scrap-metal plate to the front entrance post. A broad owner-colour patch in #d9534f and a filled household disc distinguish occupancy from the free lot's empty hoop. Hand-paint the exact player name in large, simple sand-coloured lettering on a dark weathered field. Use a few chunky bolts and a timber backing; the plate is neither an electronic display nor a clean modern estate sign.
rules.lighting: Street light: 14 parts at x 0, z 5. A concrete-and-tyre footing supports a crooked salvaged pipe mast, a short crossarm, exposed cable loops and three dim warm bulbs under mismatched tin shades. Include a small unlit battery box at the base. Only bulb parts use glow=true; shades, cables, switches and battery fittings do not emit. Use short bulb strings only at gathering points, never a luminous street network. Overall lighting is warm, low-angle dusty daylight, slightly dimmer than the Modern Age, with enough soft fill to read faces and dark entrances; haze belongs mainly in the distance.
rules.centrepiece: Use 48 parts within a roughly 4.5 m diameter for a communal fire barrel, three low scrap seats and a working junk wind turbine. The central oil drum has a broad open top, small chunky flames and a protective low scrap-metal collar. Offset the turbine mast to the rear of the gathering circle; give it a stable salvaged-concrete footing, three broad mismatched sheet-metal blades and a simple tail vane, with the hub about 3 m high. Run a visible cable to an unlit battery box and a short string of three dim bulbs above one seating edge. Keep the mast slender, the rotor modest and the circle's front open so people remain visible. Only flames and bulbs use glow=true; there is no glowing rotor, fountain basin, water jet or smoke curtain.
rules.seating: Use 10 parts for a two-person salvaged vehicle bench seat bolted to a timber crossbeam on low tyre supports. Give the broad seat faded olive upholstery, one large stitched patch and an uneven but intact backrest. The sitting surface is about 0.45 m high. Keep it stable and welcoming, without sharp protrusions, exposed springs or the silhouette of a modern park bench.
rules.market: Use 32 parts within about 2.6 × 1.6 m for a barter stall under a sagging patched tarp. Two pipe uprights and two timber posts support a broad sand-and-olive canopy with visible corner ties. A reclaimed door laid across low oil drums forms the counter, backed by one corrugated-metal windbreak. Display water cans, unbranded food tins, bundled cloth, spare bolts, a seed tray and simple repair tools in shallow crates. Preserve a clear serving side and tangible counter; no glass-fronted kiosk, electronic till, glowing labels or decorative weapon rack.
rules.trees: Street pair: 28 parts total at x -3 and x 3, z 5. One is a taller leaning drought-stressed tree with a broken upper fork and two unequal masses of dusty olive leaves; the other is a shorter crooked fruit tree with a denser crown on one side and a single timber prop. Low tyre watering collars and patched irrigation cans show survivor care, not municipal landscaping. Wild group: 36 parts for a tall wind-bent snag with a little surviving foliage, a broad low thorn tree with an off-centre canopy, and a squat irregular sage-like bush. Keep trunks tilted, branch lengths unequal and crown heights distinct; not every plant is dead. Countryside dressing: 16 low, scattered parts of straw-coloured grass, pale stones, broken twigs, flattened dry scrub, two small concrete fragments and a half-buried tyre section, mostly below 0.35 m. Leave generous calm ground between features; no junk carpet, crystals or tall ruin walls.
rules.arrival: Use 68 parts for a survivor pickup stop and an armoured scrap bus. At z 5, make a narrow waiting shelter from two salvaged posts, a corrugated roof and a patched rear tarp, with a short tyre-supported seat and a hand-painted bus-wheel pictogram on scrap metal. At z 0, aligned along x, place a toy-compressed bus about 5 m long, rebuilt with a shortened passenger cabin, an external bracing frame, broad mismatched armour plates, chunky rubber tyres and a roof rack carrying secured water cans. Keep recognisable passenger windows, a front windscreen and a side boarding door facing +z, with a clear step and route to the shelter. This is a reconstructed transport machine, not an intact modern minibus with a rust texture. Headlamps are off; omit guns, spikes, smoke plumes and hovering.
rules.crossing: Use 64 parts for a survivor-repaired bridge running along z, about 4 m wide, resting on surviving concrete abutments and squat piers. Salvaged steel beams carry broad timber planks and flat metal repair plates, creating a continuous crossing with no holes or raised obstacles. Low mismatched pipe rails and tyre buffers protect the edges without hiding travellers. The deck meets the banks about 1 m above water. Water flows along x across |z| <= 7; the river tile displays its central 12 m, while bank landings continue to z ±7 in the adjoining bank sections. Dress the banks with dull reeds, silt, concrete chunks and a few sandbags. The water is opaque murky olive-grey, with broad subdued ripples and no luminous contamination, bright foam or rainbow oil sheen.
rules.camp: Use 88 parts for the scrap convoy's camp across the river beyond the east ring road. Include two grounded armoured rigs with large rubber tyres, reinforced cabs, external load frames and visibly secured cargo. One carries a shortened shipping-container sleeping pod; two patched tarp lean-tos beside the rigs complete the three shelters. Arrange water drums, spare tyres, timber crates, bundled metal stock and a small repair table around a low fire barrel, keeping a clear entrance and central meeting space. A short string of dim bulbs hangs under one tarp; only flames and bulbs use glow=true. Use compact sheltered arrangements rather than a threatening war camp. The separate caravan leader uses 42 parts including the base figure: a road boss in a long patched dust coat, padded scrap shoulder pieces, heavy boots, a cloth-wrapped cap with unlit goggles, and a cross-body travel satchel. Give them a rolled route chart and a cluster of faded unfamiliar convoy pennants on the satchel, suggesting distant roads without tiny text, modern tourist stickers or glowing navigation devices.
rules.people: Use 50 parts total for two residents at x -0.6 and x 0.6, retaining the supplied blocky base bodies and friendly readable faces. One wears patched ochre overalls over a faded shirt, reinforced work boots and a soft cap with dark hair visible beneath it, and carries a large repair spanner. The other wears an olive utility coat, a sand-coloured neck scarf, patched trousers and a floppy repaired sun hat over a side braid, and carries a watering can. Build clothes from broad fabric panels, one or two obvious repairs and useful pockets. Preserve distinct silhouettes and varied skin tones without ash-covered faces, horror mutations, all-over armour or tiny cluttered survival gear.
rules.head: The Overseer uses 46 parts including the base figure. Give them a broad asymmetric scrap-plate mantle over a long faded-ochre utility coat, substantial boots and a distinctive flat-topped patched work cap with visible grey hair beneath it. The mantle is a few large rust-and-olive plates with softened corners, not powered armour. A salvaged shoulder radio with a short antenna and an oversized ring of town keys held at the waist are the dominant symbols of office. Put the shared four-node town emblem on a broad chest plate so their authority reads as stewardship of the settlement. The radio display remains dark; no crown, mayoral sash, pristine uniform, glowing visor or weapon is needed.

designDirection: The modern world has fallen: rebuild every requested object as useful survivor-made infrastructure from salvaged structure, rusty corrugated metal, scrap timber, tyres and patched cloth, never as a contemporary asset with a distress filter or a shiny future object. Preserve the 5×5 town plan, 16 m parcels, four central community lots and caravan camp across the river beyond the east ring road, with every transformation retaining its footprint and purpose. Use chunky low-poly toy silhouettes for the roughly 40° overhead camera, broad muted material patches, calm low-contrast ground and warm dusty daylight slightly dimmer than the Modern Age; reserve glow exclusively for sparse fire and dim bulbs. A skyscraper becomes a braced remnant frame filled with stacked container homes and visible stairs, a car becomes a compact four-wheeled scrap buggy with a real cab and repaired suspension, and a café becomes a container cantina with a patched tarp, kettle and physical serving hatch. Keep the settlement cosy and resourceful through tended seedlings, repaired seats, clear entrances and communal gathering spaces, not through pristine surfaces, saturated colour or technological spectacle.
